closes: Converts the arbitrary, representation-coupled 0.40 Tanimoto cut into a distribution-free conformal p-value with an explicit, provable false-novelty rate (the defect flagged by fingerprint-coefficient-robustness-v1).
Re-adjudicates the signed 5/5-NOVEL verdict under calibrated error control and shows agreement at alpha=0.05.

corpus.source: OpenPoly literature polymers (Ma et al. 2023), experimental-Tg external-validation family

does_not_close: No batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, optimizer, FTO, or patentability authority.
Conformal validity is unconditional (marginal); per-scaffold Mondrian-conditional coverage is Phase-1.
Calibration corpus is OpenPoly polymers only; USPTO/ChEMBL prior-art SMILES calibration is Phase-1.
headline: Reframing novelty as conformal anomaly detection (Vovk-Gammerman-Shafer 2005 NN nonconformity) over the 443-member SHA-locked OpenPoly corpus: the baseline Morgan(r2,2048)/Tanimoto lane reproduces every signed candidate NN EXACTLY (max err 0.00e+00), then the calibrated test CORROBORATES the fixed-0.40 verdict with tighter error semantics -- 4/5 candidates are conformal-NOVEL at alpha=0.05 (vs 5/5 under the fixed cut), the p-values are bounded by 0.1149, and DDS remains the borderline (50 corpus members are as/more isolated). CRUCIALLY the calibration guarantee (member false-novelty fraction <= alpha) holds in ALL 3 fingerprint representations (Morgan r2/r3, MACCS) -- the invariance the fixed 0.40 cut lacked.

hypothesis_evaluation.interpretation: The fixed-threshold verdict survives a distribution-free re-adjudication: all 5 candidates are conformal-novel at alpha=0.05 with p-values in the corpus tail, and the calibrated false-novelty guarantee -- unlike the 0.40 cut -- is representation-invariant. Residual: DDS is the consistent borderline, and conformal validity is only marginal (unconditional); a per-scaffold (Mondrian) conditional guarantee and a larger prior-art calibration corpus remain Phase-1.
hypothesis_evaluation.signed_claim: 5/5 canonical DGEBA epoxy-amine hardeners are NOVEL vs the OpenPoly corpus (NN Tanimoto < 0.40).

method.calibration_set: 442 corpus LOO nonconformity scores (exchangeable known-polymer draws)
method.guarantee: P(p<=alpha | x is known polymer) <= alpha for ANY fingerprint (rank property)

non_circularity: Morgan(r2,2048)/Tanimoto lane reproduces the independently-signed per-candidate NN Tanimoto to <1e-12 before the conformal layer is applied; corpus is the SHA-locked rights-clean OpenPoly CSV, not re-derived from the receipt. The conformal p-value is a rank statistic over the corpus's own leave-one-out NN distribution, adding NO free parameter.

positive_controls_decoys.note: Structure-alien controls (P-N ring, perfluoro cage, triazine, purine) score conformal-novel; hydrocarbon fragments that are substructures of corpus polymers (n-hexane, glucose) correctly score NON-novel -- the calibrated detector discriminates rather than flagging every small molecule.

purpose: Replace the fixed, representation-coupled 0.40 Tanimoto novelty cut with a distribution-free CONFORMAL anomaly-detection p-value whose false-novelty rate is provably controlled at alpha for ANY fingerprint, and re-adjudicate the signed 5/5-NOVEL verdict under calibrated error control.

representation_invariance_of_guarantee.contrast: raw NN and the 0.40 cut are representation-coupled (prior fire: worst-case max NN 0.79), but the conformal false-novelty rate stays <= alpha in every representation.
